subject: gov.policy
name: ICT sector strategic plan
milestone: Replaced the 2018 to 2024 plan, covering 2024/25 to 2028/29
position_start: In force, aligned to the second national strategy for transformation
position_end: The same, with nine outcomes to 2029 including all government services online, and no progress report against them held
note: the held body is a front-matter extract and the artefact is the record

subject: gov.policy
name: Legacy-network retirement plan
milestone: The government approved a phased retirement plan
position_end: Third-generation service off nationwide from June 2027, with December 2028 the working date for the older network, expressly conditional, and operators running trial shutdowns during 2026
note: in March 2026 the ministry had opened talks with device importers with no firm timeline

subject: gov.policy
name: Ministerial instructions on ICT procurement
position_end: In force, requiring public institutions to host critical systems at the national data centre, and still cited by the current implementation guidelines

subject: gov.policy
name: National AI risk-assessment and harms-monitoring body
position_end: Participants reported that no dedicated national organisation conducts risk assessments, evaluations or active monitoring of errors and harms, while the technology is embedded in payments, judiciary filing, identity verification and service delivery
note: qualitative workshops, not a survey, and the report claims no representativeness

subject: gov.policy
name: National artificial intelligence agency
milestone: Cabinet approval 2026-06-08; coordinating mandate for shared compute stated 2026-08-17
position_end: Approved by cabinet to coordinate development, adoption, investment and governance, and now being asked by early-stage firms to solve infrastructure and market-access problems it has no published mandate or budget for
sources: 2026-08-17-newtimes-ai-agency-startups|2026-08-17-rwanda-startups-national-ai-agency-infrastructure-gaps|2026-06-08-ai-agency-cabinet-approves-ktpress|2026-06-10 Rwanda Launches Dedicated AI Agency to Drive Investment and Innovation
note: software developers and early-stage startups welcomed the agency in the national press and set out what they want from it - compute and infrastructure improvements, and expanded private-sector opportunity for commercialisation. That is a statement of the gaps the sector reports rather than of the agency's remit: no establishing instrument, budget, staffing or timetable is held, so the base cannot say whether any of it falls to the agency at all

subject: gov.policy
name: National artificial intelligence policy
position_start: Adopted, roughly 70% skills-focused, with no dedicated implementing institution
position_end: The same policy, now with a cabinet-approved national agency to implement it and an independent baseline placing the country among two in the region with an adopted instrument

subject: gov.policy
name: National data-sharing policy implementation
position_start: Approved and open by default, with no governance unit established and no platform
position_end: In implementation, with a data governance unit staffed under a seconded project lead building classification standards, quality standards, templates and cataloguing tools
sources: 2026-05-07 What will determine the success of Rwanda’s data governance push|2025-10-27 Introduction to the Rwanda National Data Sharing Policy
note: the policy text and its seven annexes are not held

subject: gov.policy
name: Review framework for commercial AI partnerships
milestone: A three-year vendor memorandum signed February 2026 without one
position_end: No parliamentary, multilateral or civil-society review is triggered by a commercial partnership because none exists
sources: 2026-03-17 Anthropic is Becoming the Backbone of Rwanda's Government. But Who is Accountable|2026-02-17-anthropic-rwanda-mou-ai-health-education
note: external commentary, attributed not adopted

subject: gov.legislate
name: Access to information law (Law 04/2013)
position_start: In force since 2013, with no revision announced
position_end: In force and under revision alongside the media law, on the government's own statement to an international review

subject: gov.legislate
name: Application software security directives
position_end: Issued, operationalising security by design across the software development lifecycle for internet and intranet-accessible applications in public and private institutions

subject: gov.legislate
name: Central bank regulatory sandbox
position_start: Operating, with no published cohort or admission data
position_end: Still operating and cited as a sequencing model, with no cohort list, admission count or graduation figure held
sources: 2026-06-19 Strategy Ahead of Infrastructure, Part II The Opportunity and the Case for Sequencing
note: analyst-sourced; the sandbox's own regulation is not held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Competition and consumer protection law (Law 011/2026)
milestone: Enacted 26 February 2026, repealing the 2012 competition law
position_end: In force, its sixth chapter creating the first dedicated statutory e-commerce framework — enterprise and intermediary obligations, licensing and online-consumer rights

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cybercrimes law
milestone: In force since 2018 and listed as operative by the cyber authority
position_end: In force, covering offences, service-provider duties, investigation powers and critical-infrastructure protection, and named as operative by the national cybersecurity strategy

subject: gov.legislate
name: Draft law governing the central bank
milestone: Relevance approved by the Chamber of Deputies, 12 February 2026
position_end: At draft stage, with its article 69 making publication of statistical and financial data and studies an express obligation of the central bank

subject: gov.legislate
name: Draft law on virtual assets
milestone: Gazetted May 2026 as the first dedicated virtual-asset legislation
position_end: Gazetted in May 2026 as the country's first dedicated legislation regulating virtual-asset businesses, with the Capital Market Authority the primary licensing and supervisory authority for virtual-asset service providers; the authority is benchmarking the framework against the United Arab Emirates', a delegation having concluded a study tour there including a two-day visit to Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority, and the two regulators have begun work towards a memorandum of understanding
note: no gazette number, licence granted or supervised provider is on record, and the UAE side frames the cooperation as part of an initiative to expand regulatory partnerships with emerging markets across Africa

subject: gov.legislate
name: Single digital identification law
milestone: A June 2027 sunset of all legacy documents written into the law
position_start: In force, with nationwide enrolment not yet opened
position_end: Enrolment open and scaling, with banks, hospitals, telecoms operators and government institutions expected to use the new authentication from the sunset date and legacy cards becoming invalid
sources: 2026-03-26-govt-sets-2027-deadline-digital-id-newtimes|2025-08-08 Rwanda National Identification Agency begins digital ID enrollment
note: the law's number and enactment date are not held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Single digital identity law (Law 029/2023)
position_end: In force, governing population registration in the single digital identity system, defining authentication, requiring relying-party integration and requiring synchronisation with civil registration

subject: gov.legislate
name: Statistical activities law (Law 45/2013)
milestone: In force since 2013 and still cited on the statistics institute's legal page
position_end: In force, founding the national statistical system and assigning the statistics institute its coordinating role

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection and privacy law
position_start: In force and in its enforcement phase since October 2023, with no published enforcement record
position_end: In force with extraterritorial reach and fines to RWF 5m or 1% of global turnover, still with no enforcement action, fine total or breach register published
sources: 2026-01-26-year-of-accountability-data-controllers-newtimes|2026-05-18 Africa’s Digital Economy Is Expanding Faster than Its Privacy Protections
note: the Act's own text and law number are not held

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection appropriation
position_start: RWF 130m for 2025/26, down from RWF 150m, with no outturn published
position_end: RWF 130m again for 2026/27, with the 2024/25 outturn now known at RWF 52.71m against RWF 150m enacted, 35.1%, all in the first quarter
note: about US$114,000 at the 2024/25 rate

subject: gov.protect
name: Data sharing arrangement under the health memorandum
milestone: Terms read off the signed memorandum by a rights organisation, 2026-06-08
position_end: A rights organisation's reading of the seven signed American health memoranda puts Rwanda among three that commit to hand over any data requested for the American audit without explicit privacy safeguards, and among five whose text requires unilateral sharing of specimens and pathogen-sequencing data; all seven require broad audit access
note: the arrangement itself is not published; the reading is one organisation's of the signed memorandum text

subject: gov.protect
name: Data-protection supervisory authority
milestone: Named supervisory authority under the 2021 law
position_start: The supervisory authority, budgeted inside the presidency, in an awareness phase
position_end: A capacity-building phase with more than a hundred public-sector officers trained, authorising every cross-border transfer

subject: gov.protect
name: Privacy compliance score
position_end: 33% for 2025, level with one neighbour, against 46% for another and a 46% continental average
sources: 2026-05-18 Africa’s Digital Economy Is Expanding Faster than Its Privacy Protections
note: a third-party scorecard; no country-specific 2024 figure held

subject: gov.protect
name: Registered data controllers and processors
milestone: A registration regime live since the 2021 law
position_end: Still no count of registered controllers or processors, and no enforcement or fine total
note: the authority's own framing is that registration is the beginning, not the end

subject: gov.protect
name: Restriction on social media use by minors
position_end: A restriction on social media use by under-16s in preparation, one of several African measures moving from a minimum age for opening an account towards design duties on the platforms themselves, against an African Union child online safety policy of 2024 asking states to require protection by design and by default, risk assessments, personal-data safeguards, researcher access to platform data and independent oversight
note: no draft text, sponsoring body or timetable is named in the account held, and the constraint reported across the region is enforcement rather than law

subject: gov.protect
name: United States bilateral health agreement and its data-sharing agreement
milestone: Signed at Washington 2025-12-05 by Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe; text republished by Public Citizen
position_end: Signed memorandum with activities running 2026-04-01 to 2030-12-31; section 2.5.2 commits Rwanda to negotiate a further 25-year data-sharing arrangement with no data-owner clause or volume cap, unlike Uganda's equivalent instrument

subject: gov.regional
name: Bilateral licence passporting memorandum
position_start: Signed, with the text unpublished so the licence categories it recognises are unknown
position_end: Still unpublished by either central bank as at 2026-07-30, cited as a working precedent with no firm reported as having used it

subject: gov.regional
name: COMESA regional AI framework
milestone: Kigali country consultations held 2026-08-03 under COMESA's IDEA Programme
position_end: Consultation stage only; findings to feed a regional study toward a Regional AI Strategy, Model Policy Guidelines and Model Regulatory Frameworks; no text or timetable published; Rwanda participates as host, reporting unquantified progress on its own national AI policy

subject: gov.regional
name: Cross-border digital identity pilot
milestone: Pilot running with Ghana and Benin
position_end: A pilot recognising a digital identity issued in one of Rwanda, Ghana and Benin in the other two, presented as the first step to a single African digital market by 2030, with eighteen further countries said to be joining
note: run through a continental alliance with German development cooperation; no scale, service, date or governing instrument is stated

subject: gov.standards
name: Cross-border data-exchange conformance
milestone: The capital hosted a technical assessment mission April 2026
position_end: Identification, immigration and technology authorities convened with two other states on trust chains, interface contracts and cross-border verification toward a federated architecture, with no national conformance profile or adoption instrument held
sources: 2026-04-27 Smart Africa drives cross-border data interoperability through SADX Technical Mission
note: the country here is host and participant; the framework itself belongs on the region's ledger

subject: gov.standards
name: Electronic-government interoperability framework
milestone: Rwanda Government-wide Enterprise Architecture Framework (RGEA) v2.1 document acquired (excerpt)
position_end: RGEA v2.1, published by RISA and based on TOGAF, in force to govern government-wide ICT architecture standards; distinct from the 2019 dissertation's named 'interoperability framework', which the base still holds no separate instrument for
sources: 2019-10-01 E-Government Systems Interoperability Challenges - Public Sector in Rwanda (Mugumya, MSc thesis)|2026-08-06-risa-government-of-rwanda-enterprise-architecture-framework-v2-1
note: a reference study, cited not absorbed

subject: gov.standards
name: Gazetted national standards
position_end: Standards from two 2025 board sessions gazetted across agriculture, food, packaging, chemicals and cosmetics, with one information-technology entry among them
note: The catalogue is overwhelmingly non-digital; the digital content is a single committee entry

subject: gov.standards
name: Mutual recognition arrangements with neighbouring standards bodies
milestone: Signed with two national bodies, March 2026
position_end: Signed with the Congolese and Zimbabwean standards bodies, operationalising cross-border recognition on a one standard, one test, one certificate basis

subject: gov.standards
name: Standards board law (Law 50/2013)
milestone: Constituted the standards board, repealing the earlier framework
position_end: In force, establishing the standards board and its mandate to set and publish national standards

subject: gov.discourse
name: Citizens' assembly guidelines
position_start: Weekly assemblies, reporting outside a digital channel
position_end: Revised to twice-weekly assemblies with reporting formally routed through the electronic citizen complaints system

subject: gov.discourse
name: Governance and decentralisation sector strategic plan
position_end: In force, and stating in its own self-assessment that existing dialogue forums have not yet translated into effective influence over policy and budgeting

subject: gov.discourse
name: Internet governance forum
position_end: An annual multistakeholder forum run under the domain registry, with nearly 200 people through a school on internet governance and a youth forum
note: no outcome document, government commitment or first-edition date held

subject: gov.discourse
name: National Dialogue Council
position_start: Nineteen sessions held, with resolutions unpublished for this cycle
position_end: Resolutions published from the twentieth session, including a governance resolution requiring performance contracts to reflect citizens' concerns more closely

subject: finance.budget
name: Education technology appropriation, second line
position_end: RWF 832,894,405 for 2026/27, down 34.4% year on year and 74% against 2024/25
note: the 2024/25 year spent 252.4% of its revised allocation

subject: finance.budget
name: Education technology integration appropriation
position_end: RWF 28,956,710,022 for 2026/27, up 23.1%, with the last outturn at 81.7% of voted
note: the one education technology line that grows

subject: finance.mou
name: Capital markets registrar-services memorandum with Africa Prudential
position_end: Signed between the Capital Markets Authority and a Nigerian registrar company to cooperate on registrar services, securities administration, investor identification, data management and digital capital-markets systems, following a study visit in June 2026 to that company's digital investor-services model of virtual shareholder meetings, electronic voting and mobile-based investment tracking
note: no term, value or workplan is published, and no investor-data protection provision is reported

subject: finance.new
name: Digital acceleration project, inclusion components
position_start: An envelope of about US$200m, 55% complete
position_end: Still 55%, with no updated disbursement or completion figure and the project period ending in 2026
note: the device fund, ambassador expansion and school and clinic connectivity sit here

subject: finance.new
name: Financing agreements for broadband and labour-market systems
milestone: Approved unanimously by the Chamber of Deputies 2026-08-20
position_end: Two financing agreements worth a combined Rwf279 billion approved, funding national strategy measures that include broadband expansion, a labour market information system linking job seekers to employers, and technology for livestock traceability
note: the digital share of the combined total is not itemised, and no disbursement or procurement is on record

subject: finance.new
name: Regional bank digital acceleration operation
position_start: A US$100m commitment with a US$60.5m digital access and inclusion component
position_end: Unchanged; no disbursement figure held at any date and the period closes in 2026
note: the lender's first digital investment in the sub-region

subject: finance.new
name: Social protection transformation project
milestone: Seventh implementation status report, archived 1 November 2025
movement: Advanced, disbursement at 5.5% with fourteen months to closing
position_end: US$5.53m disbursed of the US$100m credit, 5.53%, with US$94.47m undisbursed against a 31 December 2026 closing date
note: the project finances the work the dynamic social registry sits in

subject: infra.connect
name: Country partnership framework
position_start: A framework in force for 2021 to 2026 with an indicative US$912m first-cycle allocation
position_end: A nine-year framework prepared but not launched, with job creation the organising objective and no committed envelope on the record

subject: infra.connect
name: Cross-border terrestrial fibre route
position_end: A 2,000 km protected terrestrial route across four countries, live and carrying wholesale traffic with direct interconnection into data centres in each city. Its operator marked a first year in the country in August 2026, describing a 2,000km protected corridor from Goma to Mombasa connecting Kigali, Kampala and Nairobi within a network spanning sixteen African countries
note: a vendor press release republished verbatim, with no independent confirmation the route is live; the corridor length and the network footprint are the operator's own announcement

subject: infra.connect
name: Digital acceleration project
position_start: A US$200m World Bank commitment for 2022 to 2026, 55% complete with US$47.2m disbursed
position_end: The same, with no progress or completion figure published since July 2025 against a December 2026 closing date
note: the largest connectivity instrument in the base and the one with the stalest reporting

subject: infra.connect
name: Excise duty on mobile services
milestone: Stepped from 12 to 14 per cent in June 2026
position_end: 14 per cent from June 2026, within an effective average tax rate on mobile-sector pre-tax profits put at 74 to 83 per cent
note: An operators' trade association's own commissioned analysis, held as that party's argument

subject: infra.connect
name: Fifth-generation network
position_end: The same, with no coverage, site count or subscriber figure published since
sources: 2025-06-12 Rwanda hits 38% internet penetration, but cost still keeps millions offline
note: nothing on the build has entered the base in fourteen months

subject: infra.connect
name: Government network
milestone: Named as a subcomponent carrying US$33.5m
position_start: A planned resilient national government network linking institutions to cell level
position_end: The same, with no build, coverage or completion figure published
note: a named national system that has not moved in the base in twelve months

subject: infra.connect
name: Information and communications for development appropriation
milestone: Domestic appropriation falls a third year running
position_start: RWF 5,395,372,252 domestic against RWF 45.06bn external for 2025/26
position_end: RWF 4,851,958,667 domestic against RWF 65,798,446,317 external for 2026/27
note: the programme is now 93% externally financed and rising

subject: infra.connect
name: Internet penetration
milestone: An international body put mid-2025 at 38%, with end-2025 projected at 42.6%
position_end: 42.6% projected for end-2025 with 1.35m households on home internet, and no measured 2026 figure published
sources: 2025-06-12 Rwanda hits 38% internet penetration, but cost still keeps millions offline|2025-10-22-digital-penetration-masterclass-telecomreview
note: the most recent penetration number in the base is a projection, not a measurement

subject: infra.connect
name: Mobile and internet subscriptions
milestone: Regulator quarterly statistics for the first quarter of 2026
position_start: 13,194,764 mobile-cellular and 10,064,499 internet subscriptions a year earlier
position_end: 14,001,080 mobile-cellular subscriptions at 97.1 per 100 inhabitants and 10,738,906 internet subscriptions
note: the report carries no printed publication date

subject: infra.connect
name: Mobile voice and data tariffs
milestone: Published for the fourth quarter of 2025
movement: No change, a level restated rather than moved
position_end: RWF 40 a minute for voice and RWF 10 or 5 per megabyte for data, on the regulator's own quarterly figures

subject: infra.connect
name: National broadband policy
milestone: Revised in 2022, abandoning the single-wholesale-network model
position_start: A technology-neutral policy in force with operators refarming spectrum
position_end: The same, with additional spectrum allocated across multiple operators

subject: infra.connect
name: New subsea cable system
milestone: Announced early July 2026, no timeline given
position_end: A 25,000 km system with 48 fibre pairs and twenty landing points across fifteen countries, reached from Rwanda over terrestrial fibre rather than a landing
sources: 2026-07-09 Seacom plans 25,000km subsea cable from France to Singapore and South Africa
note: a landlocked country's exposure is backhaul, so the row moves only if the terrestrial leg is contracted

subject: infra.connect
name: Regional communications satellite feasibility study
milestone: Joint funding account opened, deposits due 30 September 2026
position_end: Uganda, Kenya, Rwanda and South Sudan opened a joint bank account to fund a feasibility study for a regional communications satellite, taking partner-state contributions with a 30 September 2026 deadline to deposit and launch the study, under the roadmap settled at the April 2026 Nairobi meeting
note: neither the study's cost nor each state's share was disclosed

subject: infra.connect
name: Rwanda internet exchange point
milestone: A new cloud operator connected, June 2026
position_end: Operating under a regulator and registry memorandum, taking a new cloud-infrastructure member in June 2026, with the country selected to host the continental peering forum in August 2026

subject: infra.connect
name: Satellite reseller authorisation
milestone: Certified by the space agency, partnership since December 2025
position_end: A certified reseller with packages for health, education and non-profits and small-business plans planned
note: the held body is partial and flagged for verification

subject: infra.connect
name: Second-generation network switch-off
milestone: December 2028 stated as a government working target
position_end: A target rather than a fixed deadline, conditional on the earlier shutdown's outcome, coverage, service continuity, legacy-handset counts and migration of dependent systems
note: a commissioned study puts more than two million people still on the older network in 2030 absent a planned transition

subject: infra.connect
name: Shared tower investment
milestone: A development institution committed US$44.4m September 2025
position_end: US$44.4m of equity into shared tower infrastructure leased to mobile operators, aimed at underserved rural coverage
note: a multi-market vehicle, with no country-specific tower count held

subject: infra.connect
name: Telecommunication infrastructure sharing regulation
position_end: In force, requiring cost-based, non-discriminatory infrastructure sharing — a structural route to lower retail prices through less duplicated network investment

subject: infra.connect
name: Third-generation network switch-off
position_end: A nationwide shutdown fixed for 2027-06-30, with pilot shutdowns in selected areas during 2026 and critical-system migration completed in the first half of 2027; extensions temporary and regulator-approved
sources: 2026-07-28-rwanda-minict-3g-2g-network-sunset|2026-07-29-rwanda-june-2027-deadline-retire-3g|2026-03-30 Rwanda Moves to Phase Out 2G and 3G Devices in Digital Transition Push
note: the stated rationale is operator cost and spectrum, not consumer benefit

subject: infra.connect
name: Voice over fourth-generation networks
position_end: Voice over fourth-generation networks live for compatible handsets, with no coverage, handset-base, subscriber figure or completion date published
note: the technical precondition for retiring circuit-switched voice, though the source makes no reference to the sunset

subject: infra.store
name: African-founded cloud and artificial-intelligence infrastructure providers
milestone: Providers named in a continental roundup, August 2026
position_end: A generation of African-founded cloud and artificial-intelligence infrastructure providers is emerging against dependence on hyperscale platforms based in the United States and Europe, offering sovereign and low-latency alternatives
note: an outlet's roundup rather than a market measure; no capacity, customer count or domestic share is stated

subject: infra.store
name: Commercial tier III data centre licence
position_end: A fifteen-year licence granted covering cloud hosting, storage, disaster recovery and backup infrastructure

subject: infra.store
name: Data centre and cloud service directives
milestone: Issued 2023, dated only by the ministry's sector plan
position_end: The same; the directives' own text carries no date on its face and no compliance or enforcement record is published
note: the directives govern the national facility, and the sector plan is what dates them

subject: infra.store
name: Data centre memorandum with a Gulf operator
milestone: Second memorandum with a Gulf operator signed, reported 2026-08-19
position_end: Two memoranda to jointly invest in AI-ready Tier III data centres with Gulf operators, the later one announced in the week to 19 August 2026, with no site, capacity, cost, financing or date published for either
note: memoranda, not financed builds; the two are with related Omani entities and the record does not say whether they describe the same facility

subject: infra.store
name: Digital adoption implementation guidelines
position_end: In force, setting government-wide hardware, software, hosting and disaster-recovery requirements and mandating off-site backup at the national data centre across four recovery tiers

subject: infra.store
name: Digital investment roadmap
milestone: Launched at an investment conference October 2025
position_end: A ministry roadmap with international partners on policy and regulatory reforms to attract cloud, financial-technology and data-infrastructure investment
note: no reform has been reported as enacted since

subject: infra.store
name: Hybrid cloud deployment
position_end: A hyperscaler hybrid-cloud deployment live with a delivery partner, the government and the information society authority, the first in the region and third on the continent
sources: 2026-04-17 Amazon Web Services launches Outposts in Rwanda. - Montjalinews|2026-04-01 Rwanda hosts first AWS Outposts
note: deployment count and host facilities undisclosed, and it is the only onshore compute the base can name

subject: infra.store
name: Memorandum on a second tier III data centre
position_end: A cross-border memorandum to co-invest in a second artificial-intelligence-ready tier III data centre, with no sum stated for either party

subject: infra.store
name: National data centre
milestone: Named in the ministry's sector plan for 2024 to 2029
position_start: A national facility in operation, with no capacity or utilisation figure held
position_end: The same, with a 50% hosting-price cut recorded and 14.9% of 4,660 government websites and web applications hosted in the country
note: no capacity, load or ownership figure published, and the country hosted no hyperscale facility as at March 2026

subject: infra.store
name: Shared government data hub and interoperability platform
position_end: At pre-procurement stage, specified as a hybrid model with an on-premise national data centre core and cloud components for scalable and graphics-processing workloads

subject: infra.energy
name: Data-centre water policy
milestone: No instrument identified; an analyst calls for early planning
position_end: None published; the argument is that cooling-water use should be planned before capacity scales
note: the only country-specific energy source the base holds

subject: infra.energy
name: Electricity quality of service regulation
position_end: In force, making interruption duration and frequency indices an official, monitored and enforceable category

subject: infra.energy
name: Household electricity access
position_end: 84.6% of households connected - 59.6% to the national grid and 25.0% through off-grid systems, mainly solar
note: the utility own cumulative figure, with district rates ranging from 63.4% to 98.0%

subject: infra.energy
name: Second sustainable energy access programme
position_end: A USD 269 million loan explicitly targeting more reliable supply and 193,366 new grid connections over three years

subject: infra.capacity
name: Institute of computing
position_end: An affiliated institute of the national university beside an existing coding academy, offering degrees in artificial intelligence and cyber security, with the first two intakes limited to that academy's graduates
note: international university and vendor partnerships still to be established

subject: infra.capacity
name: National public key infrastructure upgrade
position_start: The existing infrastructure, with no upgrade contracted
position_end: Design, supply and installation put out to tender for an upgraded national public key infrastructure — the trust layer for signing, encryption and trusted transactions

subject: infra.capacity
name: Sovereign AI compute
milestone: No national accelerator cluster or sovereign AI cloud named
position_end: None held; regional AI products run on hyperscaler infrastructure abroad, and the hybrid-cloud deployment is the only onshore compute the base names
sources: 2026-08-01-east-africa-ai-industry-hidden-dependency|2026-04-17 Amazon Web Services launches Outposts in Rwanda. - Montjalinews
note: named-analyst opinion whose author sells sovereign AI infrastructure

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Biometric SIM registration regulation
position_start: In force, with registration verified against the national biometric database
position_end: The same, with no rollout completion, enrolment or enforcement figure published
sources: 2024-08-09 Regulation Governing SIM Card Registration in Rwanda (RURA No.18-2024)|2024-09-17 Rwanda conducts pilot to implement biometric SIM registration, verification

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cyber security centre of excellence
position_end: Operating at a university college with a cyber security academy, an innovation hub and technology labs, with vendor and donor partners
note: no enrolment, throughput or funding figure published since the opening

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cyber security standards and skills appropriation
position_end: RWF 723,676,491 for 2026/27, with the skills sub-line rising and the standards sub-line falling
note: the 2024/25 line executed at 11.5%, the weakest of the country's digital programmes

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cyberspace protection appropriation
position_end: RWF 1,609,000,000 for 2026/27, flat and wholly domestically financed, with the 2024/25 line executed at 85.6%

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National computer security incident response team
milestone: Profile published 2022-06-30 under the 2017 authority law
position_start: A division of the cyber security authority with a published constituency and statutory basis
position_end: The same, with services limited to identification, protection and detection and no caseload, resolution time or service-level target published
note: team membership is not public and no caseload or service-level figure is published

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National cyber security authority
milestone: Appropriated under the presidency for a third consecutive year
position_start: Budgeted under the presidency across two programmes
position_end: The same, with RWF 1.609bn and RWF 723.7m appropriated for 2026/27, both wholly domestic
note: budgeted inside the presidency rather than a ministry; establishing law and enforcement powers not held

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Reported digital payment fraud cases
position_start: a higher case count on a smaller volume of electronic transactions
position_end: reported fraud cases involving digital payments down 30% while electronic transactions rose

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Education data systems partnership

subject: include.divides
name: Financial inclusion of adults with disabilities
movement: Advanced, the banked share slightly lower
position_start: Of adults with disabilities in 2020, 15.0% banked, 58.0% with non-bank formal access only, 18.4% informal access only and 9.6% excluded
position_end: In 2024, 14.3% banked, 72.4% with non-bank formal access only, 5.1% informal access only and 8.1% excluded, on 11.2% of adults self-reporting a disability against 17% in 2020
note: self-reported disability, and the fall in reported prevalence between rounds is not explained in the source

subject: include.divides
name: Smart-device affordability fund
position_start: A design stage with the development bank as financial intermediary, phased pilots and social-category subsidy targeting
position_end: The same design stage, with no market assessment, pilot or disbursement figure held
note: the named device fund inside the acceleration project

subject: include.divides
name: Universal access or service fund
milestone: Presidential order gazetted 2023-05-15, repealing the 2004 order
position_start: In force under a presidential order of 12 May 2023, with each licensee's annual contribution capped at 2.5% of the turnover of each category of regulated service
position_end: The same; the operative rate is a regulatory-board decision not held, and the most recent accounts held remain 2020/21, when Frw 3,828,837,334 was spent against a Frw 6,372,536,516 budget
note: the fund has no separate legal personality and its staff sit inside the regulator; the annual activity report owed to the regulatory board by 30 September is not held for any year

subject: include.divides
name: Urban and rural internet use gap
position_start: 17% of households with internet at home nationally in 2016-17, with no urban and rural split held
position_end: 30% of households nationally in 2023-24 - 56% of urban households against 19% of rural
sources: 2025-06-12 Rwanda hits 38% internet penetration, but cost still keeps millions offline|2025-01-01-rwanda-eicv7-utilities-amenities
note: the national statistics survey is the source of the figure; the rural half of the gap is unchanged across the two rounds held
